content:
NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday revealed what was actually going through his mind in the now-viral moment when he stood stone-faced beside President Trump at a press conference earlier this month, as the president excoriated the media.

Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel, who was taping his show in New York this week, praised Mamdani for showing "incredible discipline" by keeping a straight face while Trump attacked CNN, MS NOW and Politico — after barring those outlets from the White House:

"That's really quite something," Kimmel said. "I was watching that and I thought, 'You know what, that's not a guy I'd want to play poker with.'"

Not only did Mamdani defend the press at the joint press conference, he also personally called each of the news organizations Trump had barred.

But, as Kimmel pointed out, none of it seems to have gotten under Trump's skin.

"He just seems to like you, that's it," Kimmel said. "I guess that's all that matters."

So what was going through Mamdani's mind as Trump attacked the press? Let's just call it the art of the deal — because he's been working with Trump on a major real-estate project.

"The biggest thing we've been talking about lately is Sunnyside Yard — this is a decades-in-the-making idea to put a platform over the rail yards and build 12,000 housing units," Mamdani said. "So in that moment where you zoomed in, I was thinking of 12,000 homes, 30,000 jobs, and the largest housing development since the early 1970s."

Kimmel offered up another suggestion that might help grease the deal.

"Have you ever thought about calling it Trumpyside Yard?" he joked.

"I hadn't thought of that," Mamdani said.
